head: Decisions, not just data. Inside your own walls.
body: Midgard is a sovereign, open-source platform suite: one enclosure for your data, your models and your operations. Four products, one trust boundary, zero outbound dependencies.

head: Your organisation, described once.
body: Aircraft, facilities, crew, sensor feeds — real things with real properties and links, not rows in a table. Select one and you see what it connects to, and exactly which actions a person is allowed to take on it.

head: Access is proven, not assumed.
body: Rules are written down and can be dry-run before they go live — this person, this clearance, this purpose. Nothing is permitted unless a rule proves it, and the decision itself is signed.

head: Audit is a query, not an archaeology project.
body: Every read, every write and every AI step lands in an append-only record, signed as it is written. Months later you search it the same way you search anything else.

head: Getting data in, without losing track of it.
body: Draw the route from raw source to finished dataset, or write it in code — the same pipeline either way. Every build is repeatable, versioned like source control, and carries its lineage with it.

head: Bad data stops before it reaches anyone.
body: 1,204 expectations run on every build. Three are failing here, so two projections are blocked from promotion — nobody downstream ever sees them.

head: AI that never phones home.
body: Ask a question in plain language; the answer is grounded in your own data with every claim cited back to it. Here Mimir spots a maintenance risk, drafts the fix — and then stops, because acting on it changes something real.

head: Five rails screen every input and every tool call.
body: A prompt-injection attempt is quarantined before a single tool runs; an uncited claim is stripped and the answer regenerated. 46 trips in seven days, and nothing has ever left the enclosure.

head: Many feeds, one picture everyone shares.
body: Radar, transponder, maritime and ground sources correlated into a single live view — 1,204 tracked entities, fused in four tenths of a second, with one anomaly raised for a human to look at.

head: AI ranks the options. People authorise the action.
body: 100% human-authorised. Nothing auto-executed, ever. The authorisation, the evidence behind it and what happened next become a single signed record.

head: Nothing deploys unless it proves itself.
body: Rebuilt bit-for-bit, ingredients listed, signature verified — then released to a small ring first, with health gates between rings and automatic rollback if one fails.

head: Even where the internet can't reach.
body: Nine sites here never connect to anything. They get the identical release on signed media, carried in by hand; it verifies itself offline and sends a signed receipt back.

head: No single person can do the dangerous things.
body: High-risk changes need a second, different approver — there is no super-admin. A self-approval attempt is refused, and the refusal is recorded alongside everything else.

head: Seven subsystems, one tamper-evident ledger.
body: Approvals, denials, emergency break-glass sessions and rehearsals all land in the same signed record. Zero entries escaped.

head: It works where the work happens.
body: One shared core behind phone, desktop and browser. Keys stay in the device's hardware, and the app keeps working with no signal — reconnecting merges everything back with no conflicts.

head: One boundary. Everything inside it.
body: From a single laptop to a fleet of air-gapped sites — the same releases, the same signatures, every topology. Open core, reproducible builds, and a full bill of materials with every release.
